newsitem.title: USA: Clinton mourns Shabazz, calls daughters.
newsitem.headline: Clinton mourns Shabazz, calls daughters.

text.p: President Clinton Monday mourned the death of Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, and called her family to express his sympathy.

"Hillary and I were saddened to learn of the passing of Betty Shabazz earlier today," Clinton said in a statement. "She devoted a long career to education and to uplifting women and children. She was also a loving mother and our prayers are with her family in this hour of grief."
Clinton expressed his sympathy in a telephone conversation with four of Shabazz's six daughters from Air Force One on a flight from San Francisco to Los Angeles, a spokesman said.

"He mentioned that he last saw her recently when she sat in his box at the Jackie Robinson tribute," White House spokesman Barry Toiv told reporters aboard the president's plane, referring to a baseball game in April at which the late Jackie Robinson was honoured.

Shabazz, 63, who became an educator and activist after her husband's murder, died Monday afternoon, succumbing to burns on more than 80 percent of her body in a June 1 blaze, which police say was set by her 12-year-old grandson.

Clinton, in California on a speaking and fund-raising trip, flew to Los Angeles Monday to speak on children's health care, and help Democratic Sen. Barbara Boxer raise money for her uphill reelection battle.
